QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_44

question.text: 'Tapti Growth Category II AIF' is negotiating a term sheet for a INR 50 crore investment at 15% equity. The founders are cash-strapped and push back on 2x participating liquidation preference. Mr. Shankar Rao, fund manager, wants downside protection WITHOUT penalising the founders on a strong exit. The BEST middle-ground structure is:

answer.text: Agree to 1x non-participating preference — gives INR 50 cr floor; if exit is rich, AIF converts and takes 15% pro-rata

explanation.text: The Logic: 1x non-participating is the founder-friendly middle ground: it returns capital (downside protection) on a weak exit, but on a strong exit the AIF converts and gets 15% pro-rata — no double-dip. This is now the market-standard in Indian VC Series A rounds. The Trap: 3x/5x participating are extreme positions, typically unacceptable to founders. Dropping LP removes downside protection. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests negotiation applications. Market-practice note: in 2020-2024 Indian VC deals, ~85% of Series A rounds used 1x non-participating. Manager's Pro-Tip: Preserve optionality by NOT asking for participation — when the exit is rich (6-8x), participation adds friction without meaningful economic uplift. Use it only in distressed or deeply risky deals.
